notes: Customer: large healthcare SaaS, high PII sensitivity — will not accept 3rd party model retention without controls.
Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with throughput guarantees for synchronous triage chat (target p95 < 120ms for 256-token responses under peak).
Secondary: embeddings for search and reranking; batch jobs okay to be lower priority but need predictable throughput overnight.

Capacity planning: infra team expects baseline concurrency ~250 simultaneous chat sessions at 20 TPS average, peak 800 concurrent bursts. Estimated reserved GPU footprint: 4 reserved (warm) + autoscale to 10 for bursts; prefer pre-warmed pools to avoid cold starts.

Autoscaling requirements discussed: scale-up aggressive (80% utilization trigger, <30s ramp to add instances), scale-down conservative (cool-down 15-30m, maintain warm pool of 2 instances for sub 100ms cold-start SLA), support for quota-based per-queue throttling.
Queueing/backpressure: want request queuing with max queue depth per-tenant, rejection policy with clear retry-after header; ability to prioritize routing for triage chat over embeddings batch jobs.
Routing & fallback: require automated fallback to smaller quantized model for cold capacity or region failover; must be configurable by route and observable in console.
Cost sensitivity: mid-high — willing to pay premium for guaranteed latency but need predictable monthly reserved costs for budgeting.
Quote from CTO on call: 'We cannot have a >200ms p95 during business hours for triage; otherwise ops load spikes.', emphasized need for warm pools and deterministic cold-start bounds.
POC success metrics: sustained p95 <120ms at 250 concurrent sessions for 30m sustained; autoscale actions without >10% request failures during scale events.
Open technical questions: cold-start measurement methodology (kernel compilation vs VM start), KV-cache priming strategy for pre-warm, rollback plan for failed scale events.
Procurement — timeline: legal + security packet due by 2026-04-15 to hit May budget cycle.
